sections.h2: Which office bills property tax in Pearland, TX?
sections.html:
The answer depends on which county your house sits in. Pearland spreads across Brazoria County and Fort Bend County, and the Texas Comptroller's directory lists the City of Pearland as an active taxing unit in both appraisal districts.

Brazoria County's tax office, at 451 N. Velasco St. in Angleton, lists the City of Pearland and Pearland ISD among the units it collects for. Its phone number is 979-864-1320. The Brazoria Central Appraisal District, which sets values, is at 500 N. Chenango St. in Angleton and answers at 979-849-7792. For a Fort Bend County address, the Fort Bend Central Appraisal District is at 2801 B.F. Terry Blvd. in Rosenberg, 281-344-8623. Fort Bend County's own collection list does not include Pearland, so ask where a Fort Bend-side parcel pays.

Expect more than the city and school lines on a bill. The Brazoria list includes Pearland Municipal Management District #2, Alvin Community College District, Brazoria County emergency districts, drainage districts and dozens of numbered municipal utility districts. A newer subdivision often carries a utility district charge that an older one does not.

Schools differ by address too. Brazoria County's list names Pearland ISD, Alvin ISD and Friendswood ISD among its school districts, so read the school line on your bill to see which one charges your street.

sections.h2: What did Pearland's 2026 tax rate notice say?
sections.html:
The city's 2026 notice prints a no-new-revenue rate of $0.637892 and a voter-approval rate of $0.693542 per $100 of value. The first rate would raise the same dollars as last year from properties taxed in both years. The second is the ceiling a city can adopt in most cases before voters must be asked.

sections.h2: What dates matter for Pearland property owners each year?
sections.html:
Texas runs one calendar for every taxing unit, so Pearland owners follow the same dates as owners in any other city. The key point is that value and ownership are fixed on January 1 for the whole year.

  • January 1: values are set, and the tax lien for the year attaches.
  • April 1 or soon after: appraisal notices go out for single-family homesteads. Other property follows around May 1.
  • Before May 1: apply for most exemptions.
  • May 15, or 30 days after the notice is delivered if later: protest deadline.
  • July 25: the chief appraiser certifies the roll to each taxing unit.
  • September 29 or thereabouts: last day for units to adopt rates.
  • October: bills are mailed. Tax is due by January 31 and delinquent February 1.

On February 1 a six percent penalty and one percent interest apply. The penalty adds one percent each month until it reaches 12 percent on July 1, and interest keeps adding one percent a month. A unit with an attorney contract may add up to 20 percent more.

Protest hearings before the appraisal review board begin around May 15, and the board is expected to approve the records by July 20 unless more than five percent of total value is still under protest. Keep the appraisal notice, because the protest deadline is counted from the day it was delivered when that is later than May 15.

sections.h2: How do Pearland homeowners reduce the bill?
sections.html:
Claim the homestead exemption the first year you own and live in the house. Pearland ISD must give the state's $140,000 school exemption, and an owner 65 or older, or disabled, gets $60,000 more on school tax. A city or county may add an optional percentage exemption of up to 20 percent of value, never under $5,000. Ask the city whether it has done so, because the Brazoria directory shows the units but not their exemption choices.

Once a homestead exemption is in place, the appraised value cannot climb more than 10 percent a year, starting the January after it is first granted. Seniors and disabled owners also get a school tax ceiling that can follow them to a new Texas homestead.

Disabled veterans get a separate exemption on any one property, scaled by VA rating as the Comptroller prints it:

  • 10 to 29 percent: up to $5,000
  • 30 to 49 percent: up to $7,500
  • 50 to 69 percent: up to $10,000
  • 70 to 100 percent: up to $12,000

A veteran with a 100 percent rating gets a total exemption on the residence homestead. An heir who inherited a Pearland house and is not on a recorded deed should give the appraisal district an affidavit of ownership, a death certificate, a recent utility bill and any court record citation.

sections.h2: What if I sell a Pearland house with unpaid taxes?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax rides with the lot until it is paid. The lien dates from January 1, a buyer cannot obtain clear title while delinquent tax remains, and the owner of record on that January 1 can still be sued for that year's tax after selling.

A collector may waive penalty and interest if the owner pays within 21 days of learning of the delinquency and asks in writing before the 181st day. Owners of a residence homestead can ask for a payment plan, and some collectors allow up to 36 months. Someone who appeals an appraisal must still pay the undisputed amount before the delinquency date.

If the taxing unit sues and the house is sold, a homestead can be redeemed within two years of the buyer's deed being filed, while other property has 180 days. Surplus sale money can be claimed by the former owner for two years.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about Pearland?
sections.html:
Pearland grew from 91,252 people in 2010 to 125,828 in 2020, and the July 2025 estimate is 129,930. The city covers 48.67 square miles of land, or roughly 2,585 people per square mile in 2020.

Owners hold 76.2 percent of homes. The median owned home is valued at $356,300 for 2020-2024, and median household income is $118,842. Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $2,611, and the typical commute is 32.7 minutes. About 47.1 percent of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree or higher, and 89.6 percent lived in the same house a year earlier.

faqs.q: Is Pearland in Brazoria County or Fort Bend County?
faqs.a: Both. The Comptroller's directories list the City of Pearland as a taxing unit in the Brazoria and the Fort Bend appraisal districts, so your parcel's location decides which district appraises it.

faqs.q: When is Pearland property tax delinquent?
faqs.a: Tax unpaid after January 31 is delinquent on February 1. A six percent penalty and one percent interest attach that day, and the penalty reaches 12 percent on July 1.

faqs.q: What rate does Pearland charge for 2026?
faqs.a: The city's 2026 notice prints $0.637892 as the no-new-revenue rate and $0.693542 as the voter-approval rate. Check your bill or the city finance office for the adopted rate, since the notice does not show it.

faqs.q: Can I pay Pearland property tax in installments?
faqs.a: Yes, in two cases. Anyone may split the bill into halves due November 30 and June 30. Owners 65 or older, or disabled, on a homestead may pay in four installments, and a delinquent homestead owner can ask for a plan of up to 36 months.

faqs.q: Who pays the year's tax when a Pearland house sells?
faqs.a: The January 1 owner is liable for that year's bill, even after a sale. In practice the closing statement splits the year, and unpaid tax from earlier years is paid off from proceeds so the buyer receives clear title.
